version_history.subject: [PATCH v5 0/3] mm: zswap: free cold writeback folios promptly

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 1/3] mm: swap: move LRU insertion out of the swap cache allocator
series_items.patch_summary: This patch moves the insertion of a new folio into the LRU (Least Recently Used) list out of the swap cache allocator function. This is done to allow callers of this function to act on the folio before it becomes visible for reclaim, which was not possible with the previous implementation. The change also enables zswap writeback dropbehind by preventing the buffer folio from being added to the LRU prematurely. The patch does not introduce any functional changes and only modifies the timing of when the LRU insertion occurs.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 2/3] mm: swap: drop dropbehind swap cache folios on writeback completion
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the Linux kernel's swap management to drop PG_dropbehind folios from the swap cache immediately after writeback completion, rather than waiting for reclaim to find them later. This change is similar to how file folios are handled and ensures that swap cache folios are properly cleaned up to prevent memory leaks. The patch introduces a new function, `swap_writeback_dropbehind_folio`, which takes the folio and swap cluster locks, sets the `BIO_COMPLETE_IN_TASK` flag on the write operation, and drops the folio directly from `folio_end_writeback`. This change is necessary to improve the kernel's memory management and prevent potential issues related to swap cache folios.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v5 3/3] mm: zswap: drop cold writeback folios via swap dropbehind
series_items.patch_summary: This patch optimizes the zswap writeback process by dropping cold folios from the swap cache once they are written back to disk. This is done by allocating the folio off the LRU and marking it PG_dropbehind, which allows the swap dropbehind path to free the folio after writeback completes. The patch also includes a workaround for a refault evaluation issue on writeback buffers and clears the PG_active flag after allocation to prevent bad_page() errors.

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch series optimizes zswap by promptly freeing cold writeback folios instead of leaving them for page reclaim to find and free later, which wastes a reclaim scan and keeps cold memory resident longer than necessary. The existing dropbehind mechanism is extended to swap cache folios, and zswap is modified to opt into this mechanism. Patch 1 moves LRU insertion out of the swap cache allocator, patch 2 drops dropbehind swap cache folios on writeback completion, and patch 3 allocates the writeback folio off the LRU and marks it dropbehind.

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH v4 0/3] mm: fix workingset refaults in the zswap writeback path

version_history.subject: [PATCH v4 0/3] mm: fix workingset refaults in the zswap writeback path

series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 1/3] mm: swap: move LRU insertion out of the swap cache allocator
series_items.patch_summary: This patch moves the insertion of a new folio into the LRU (Least Recently Used) list out of the swap cache allocator function. This change is necessary to allow callers of the allocator function to act on the newly allocated folio before it becomes visible for reclaim. The patch also addresses issues related to refault evaluation and zswap writeback dropbehind, where the buffer folio needs to stay off the LRU entirely. The functional changes are minimal, as each caller will add the folio to the LRU after allocation.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 2/3] mm: swap: refault on swap-in, not in the swap cache allocator
series_items.patch_summary: This patch moves the evaluation of page refaults from the swap cache allocator to the two callers that perform swap-in operations. This change prevents inflated working set statistics when zswap writeback continuously writes back compressed data. The patch also ensures that the shadow is handed back correctly in the swap cache allocation function, and fixes a potential issue with stale snapshots being used for refault evaluation.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 3/3] mm: zswap: preserve the workingset shadow across writeback
series_items.patch_summary: This patch addresses an issue in the zswap compression algorithm where the workingset shadow is lost during writeback operations, leading to inaccurate anon refault/workingset accounting. To fix this, the patch preserves the workingset shadow within zswap by parking it in the zswap tree instead of overwriting it when allocating a new buffer folio. The parked shadow is then handled at the next opportunity, whether that's during swap-in, reclaim, or slot free operations.

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch fixes two issues in the zswap writeback path that cause incorrect workingset refaults. The first issue is over-counting at writeback, where a buffer folio allocated by the shrinker is counted as a refault. The second issue is lost eviction cookies at reclaim, where the original cookie is overwritten when adding the buffer to the swap cache. To fix these issues, the patch preserves the shadow within zswap itself and moves the refault evaluation out of the swap-cache allocator into the swap-in callers. This results in a significant reduction (-48% to -59%) in workingset refaults, activations, and restores for anonymous pages.

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH v2 3/3] btrfs: downgrade the reflink source inode lock for tree walking

version_history.subject: [PATCH v2 3/3] btrfs: downgrade the reflink source inode lock for tree walking

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch modifies the behavior of reflink in Btrfs to downgrade the lock on the source inode from exclusive to shared during tree walking, reducing contention between reflinks and other file operations. The patch addresses two issues related to direct I/O: it adds a flag to prevent direct I/O writes from taking the lock shared when the source inode is being used as a reflink source, and it ensures that direct I/O reads do not block reflinks by remaining exclusive until after finishing with inode_dio_wait().

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH v2 2/3] btrfs: skip unlocked reflink source flush if the inode has writers

version_history.subject: [PATCH v2 2/3] btrfs: skip unlocked reflink source flush if the inode has writers

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch modifies the btrfs reflink code to skip optimistic unlocked flushing if there are active writers dirtying pages, as it can result in doubly writing back pages that get dirtied again before a locked flush. The change is advisory and does not guarantee against extra writeback, but helps in simple cases with long open file descriptors or mappings.

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH v2 1/3] btrfs: pre-flush reflink source before taking inode locks

version_history.subject: [PATCH v2 1/3] btrfs: pre-flush reflink source before taking inode locks

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch optimizes the reflink operation in Btrfs by pre-flushing the source file's dirty pages before taking inode locks, reducing contention between writers and readers. This is done through a single backwards pass that waits for ordered extents on the inode without locking the ordered tree. The approach taken avoids consistency errors associated with concurrent writes and allows for a common case optimization without significant infrastructure investment.

review_comments.author: Filipe Manana
review_comments.summary:
Reviewer Filipe Manana questioned the purpose of the variable orig_end, pointing out that it is not used elsewhere in the code.

Reviewer Filipe Manana questioned the necessity of introducing a new function, btrfs_reflink_ordered_extents(), to wait for ordered extents in reflink operations, pointing out that existing function btrfs_wait_ordered_range() already serves this purpose. Additionally, he noted that the current implementation waits for all ordered extents, which can slow down small-range reflinks.

Reviewer Filipe Manana noted that the current implementation of pre-flushing reflink source before taking inode locks causes unnecessary IO overhead for small range reflinks and fails to wait for compression to finish, suggesting using btrfs_fdatawrite_range() instead.
review_comments.raw_body:
What's the point of orig_end if it's not used elsehwere?
Just this:

u64 end = i_size_read(&inode->vfs_inode);

---

Why do we need another function to wait for ordered extents just for reflinks?

We have btrfs_wait_ordered_range() that does exactly the same...

Besides that, this waits for all ordered extents. If a reflink
operates on a small range, we end up waiting for any ordered extents,
which slows down such ranged reflinks.
btrfs_wait_ordered_range() allows to pass a range.

---

So again, this flushes the entire file, which adds overhead for
reflinks operating on a small range and causes unnecessary IO.

Further, using filemap_flush() is not enough in case we have compression.
The flush call only starts the compression work in an async worker, we
need a second flush call to wait for the compression to finish and for
writeback to start (creating ordered extents).
That's why we have btrfs_fdatawrite_range(), which does the double
flush in case we have compression, and also supports specifying a
range.

Thanks.

review_comments.author: Boris Burkov (author)
review_comments.summary:
Author acknowledged that their initial approach was not better, agreed that btrfs_wait_ordered_range() is a more suitable solution, and expressed inability to think of an alternative.

The author addressed a concern about the effectiveness of pre-flushing reflink source before taking inode locks, explaining that folio locking works in a way that makes this optimization unnecessary and removing it for v3.
sentiment_signals: author acknowledged a fix is needed
review_comments.raw_body:
TL;DR you are right

I started with btrfs_wait_ordered_range() then got turned around while
exploring the space and ended here which turns out to not be any better.
Thanks for pushing back.

Basically I was battling against cases related to the one helped by the
second patch (concurrent writers producing dirtying which causes write
amplification with the duplicate flush outside the locks) and tried to
create a "lightest weight good enough" flush for this application.

However, I don't think I succeeded and can't think of anything actually
better than btrfs_wait_ordered_range(). (and it's worse for using
SYNC_NONE and doing the whole file...)

---

Interestingly, this turns out to not really matter due to how the folio
locking works today (and that we don't care about 100% perfect
submission anyway). Basically the second folio gets blocked right away
in filemap_flush and waits until the first folio's async compression
finishes and unlocks it. This is the same pattern that Qu is contending
with in his parent-child OE redesign to try to make compressed writeback
look "normal".

There is 0 benefit I can demonstrate objectively from relying on this so
I am going to switch back to plain btrfs_wait_ordered_range() for v3.

version_history.subject: [PATCH v2 0/4] sched/numa: stop VMA scan filters from gating promotion

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 1/4] mm: support promotion-only NUMA hinting scans
series_items.patch_summary: This patch introduces support for promotion-only NUMA hinting scans in the Linux kernel. It adds a new flag MM_CP_PROT_NUMA_PROMO_ONLY to distinguish between placement and promotion-only scans, allowing the scanner to choose whether to promote pages or not. The change is made to the mm module, specifically in the functions change_prot_numa(), task_numa_work(), and vma_set_file(). The patch preserves existing behavior for certain fixes related to NUMA balancing and memory tiering systems.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 2/4] mm: allow shared folios to be promoted to a fast tier
series_items.patch_summary: This patch allows shared copy-on-write folios and executable file folios mapped by multiple processes to be promoted from a slow memory tier to a fast one, while maintaining existing restrictions for ordinary placement. This change is intended to improve the performance of memory tiering systems by allowing hot folios on slow tiers to be moved to faster storage. The patch modifies two kernel files, mm/mempolicy.c and mm/migrate.c, to relax the checks that previously blocked such promotions. The changes are based on a previous patch (c574bbe91703) that optimized page placement for memory tiering systems.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 3/4] sched/numa: scan read-only file mappings in tiering mode
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the NUMA (Non-Uniform Memory Access) hinting mechanism to scan read-only file mappings when memory tiering is enabled, but only for promotion purposes. This change allows hot file folios on slow memory to be tracked by the tiering code, improving performance in certain scenarios. The patch addresses an issue where shared libraries and other read-only file-backed mappings were excluded from NUMA hinting, leading to placement bouncing and poor performance. By scanning these mappings, the patch enables more accurate tracking of runtime load and improves overall system responsiveness.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 4/4] sched/numa: do not let VMA PID activity gate promotion
series_items.patch_summary: This patch prevents VMA PID activity from gating memory promotion in NUMA-aware scheduling. It introduces a new field to track the sequence ID of socket-placement scans and allows periodic placement scans to avoid starvation. The change is motivated by a scenario where a large shmem VMA occupied each scan, causing 84 GB of VMAs to be skipped as inactive. The patch fixes a previous commit that enhanced vma scanning logic and improves memory tiering in multi-threaded applications.

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch series aims to improve NUMA balancing by separating promotion-only scans from socket-placement scans, allowing eligible shared folios to be promoted and enabling read-only file mappings and PID-inactive VMAs to be scanned for promotion without re-enabling placement sampling. The changes involve adding a new protection walk flag, MM_CP_PROT_NUMA_PROMO_ONLY, and modifying the existing code to track the last placement scan separately.

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH nfs-utils v2 00/10] mountd: bugfixes for up/downcall interfaces

version_history.subject: [PATCH nfs-utils v2 00/10] mountd: bugfixes for up/downcall interfaces

series_items.subject: [PATCH nfs-utils v2 01/10] mountd: factor out the per-path export attribute computation
series_items.patch_summary: This patch refactors the code in the mountd service to factor out the computation of per-path export attributes into a separate function, `export_attrs_build`. This change is made to allow the netlink downcall to use this computation as well. The patch does not introduce any functional changes and only modifies the internal implementation of the mountd service.

series_items.subject: [PATCH nfs-utils v2 02/10] mountd: handle unmountable paths and junctions in the netlink downcall
series_items.patch_summary: This patch improves the handling of unmountable paths and junctions in the netlink downcall for NFS exports. It addresses two issues: when is_mountpoint() fails, it defers the request instead of answering 'not exported', and it checks for a junction before denying referrals. The patch splits lookup_nonexport() to share junction lookup between downcalls and factors per-request work into nl_add_export_req(). Deferred requests are retried from cache_process() every RETRY_SEC. The kernel keeps the upcall pending in the meantime.

series_items.subject: [PATCH nfs-utils v2 03/10] mountd: answer requests the kernel rejects on the netlink downcall
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the mountd service to handle rejected requests from the kernel when processing export requests via netlink downcalls. The kernel rejects certain requests, causing pending requests to be dropped and clients to hang on lookups. The patch resubmits rejected requests one at a time, answers negative for refused entries, and logs size failures. It also separates the kernel's errno from libnl errors in cache_nl_set_reqs().

series_items.subject: [PATCH nfs-utils v2 04/10] mountd: don't leak the parent export's fsid onto crossmnt submounts
series_items.patch_summary: This patch fixes an issue where cross-mount submounts inherit their parent's fsid, leading to filehandle aliasing and ESTALE errors on the client side. The patch introduces a new function `export_attrs_build` to compute export attributes, including flags, fsid, and uuid, which are then used in the `nfsd_nl_add_export` function. This change ensures that cross-mount submounts get their own filehandles and prevents the parent's fsid from being leaked onto them. The patch also includes a fallback mechanism for unresolved exports and honors the export's TTL on positive entries.

series_items.subject: [PATCH nfs-utils v2 05/10] mountd: retry unresolvable fsid lookups on the netlink downcall
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the mountd service to retry unresolvable file system ID (fsid) lookups on netlink downcalls. The fsid lookup is moved out of nfsd_handle_fh() and into a separate function, lookup_fsid(). If the fsid cannot be resolved immediately, the request is deferred and retried at regular intervals. This change addresses issues with spurious ESTALE errors and improves handling of unmounted autofs submounts. The patch also includes additional error checking and logging to prevent denial-of-service attacks.

series_items.subject: [PATCH nfs-utils v2 06/10] mountd: bound the junction path before copying it into e_path
series_items.patch_summary: This patch fixes a potential heap corruption issue in the mountd service by adding bounds checking to ensure that junction paths do not exceed the maximum allowed length before copying them into the e_path field of an exportent structure. This is done by checking the length of the junction path and rejecting it if it exceeds the limit, rather than attempting to copy it directly. The patch addresses a specific vulnerability where a malicious user could set up a trusted.junction.nfs xattr to create a deep junction path that would corrupt the heap.

series_items.subject: [PATCH nfs-utils v2 07/10] mountd: give each worker its own netlink command socket
series_items.patch_summary: This patch addresses a problem in the mountd service where multiple worker processes share the same netlink command socket, leading to incorrect handling of requests and replies. To fix this, each worker is given its own netlink command socket by reopening the inherited sockets in the child process. This ensures that each request is handled correctly and prevents two workers from taking each other's acknowledgments or error messages during a round trip.

series_items.subject: [PATCH nfs-utils v2 08/10] mountd: retry export attributes that fail to resolve for a passing reason
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the mountd service in the nfs-utils package to retry export attributes that fail to resolve due to a passing reason, such as a temporary network issue or an incomplete fsid restart. The patch introduces a new error handling mechanism where EAGAIN is returned for cases where the path cannot be determined immediately, and EINVAL is kept for genuine non-exportable paths. This change allows the mountd service to recover from temporary issues and prevents unnecessary downtime due to fsidd restarts.

series_items.subject: [PATCH nfs-utils v2 09/10] mountd: drop a deferred fsid lookup once it has been answered
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the mountd service in NFS-utils to remove a deferred file system ID (fsid) lookup once it has been answered. The patch addresses an issue where building an expkey batch can defer an entry, leading to duplicate answers from the retry queue. It introduces two new functions: `delayed_expkey_matches` and `delayed_expkey_remove`, which enable efficient removal of deferred entries from the queue. This change ensures that each entry is only answered once, preventing unnecessary retries and improving overall performance.

series_items.subject: [PATCH nfs-utils v2 10/10] mountd: bound the retry queues
series_items.patch_summary: This patch bounds the retry queues in the mountd service to prevent them from growing indefinitely. The queues are used when a client's filehandle or fsid cannot be immediately verified as exportable, and they can become large due to unmounted exports on the server. The patch introduces a cap of 1024 entries for each queue and drops new requests once this limit is reached. This change prioritizes latency over correctness, as the kernel will repeat the upcall when the client retries. Deduplication mechanisms are also added to reduce memory usage in these queues.

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch series addresses several bugs in the mountd service, including issues related to crossmnt and autofs configurations, statfs errors, and deferred fsid lookups. The patches factor out per-path export attribute computation, handle unmountable paths and junctions, answer rejected requests, prevent parent export's fsid from leaking onto submounts, retry unresolvable fsid lookups, bound the junction path, give each worker its own netlink command socket, and drop deferred fsid lookups once answered.
